example_flows.t: Lipstick: one studio shot becomes a vanity scene and a shade swatch
example_flows.d: The starting photo was a single coral lipstick on a plain studio background. From it we made a scene on a marble vanity beside a mirror and a fresh flower, and a close-up next to a swatch of the same shade, so shoppers can judge the color before they buy.

example_flows.t: Hoodie: a flat product photo becomes street style and a flat lay
example_flows.d: We started with a front view of a plain gray hoodie. From it we made an image of someone wearing it on an autumn street and a flat lay on a wooden bench with a beanie and a scarf, so the same item works on a product page and in social posts.

example_flows.t: Coffee beans: a plain bag in a kitchen and at a breakfast table
example_flows.d: We started with a photo of a kraft coffee bag with a blank label and a scatter of beans. From it we made a kitchen counter scene with a pour-over brewer and a mug, and a breakfast table with a croissant, so the product looks at home in the moments people drink it.

ugc.title: What is an AI UGC video ad?
paras: UGC stands for user-generated content. A UGC-style ad looks like a short clip a customer filmed on their phone: casual, close to the product and made for TikTok, Reels and Shorts rather than TV.

An AI UGC video ad gives you that look without hiring a creator or shipping your product to anyone. You upload a photo of your product, pick a style or describe the scene, and AIVideosUGC makes a 6, 10 or 15 second clip built around your real product.

The people in these clips are generated by AI, not real customers, so use them to show the product rather than as reviews. Captions, music and prices go on afterward in your editor or ad tool, where you control every word.

faq.q: What can I make with AIVideosUGC?
faq.a: Short video ads, product and unboxing videos, white-background photos, lifestyle photos, model photos and social ad images. Most start from a photo of your product.
A clear photo of the product you sell. A phone photo on a plain background works well. Only upload photos you own or have permission to use.

faq.q: How long are the videos, and what sizes can I get?
faq.a: Videos are 6, 10 or 15 seconds. Choose 9:16 for TikTok, Reels and Shorts, 1:1 for feeds, or 16:9 for wider placements.
You see the credit cost before you start. Credits are held when your job starts and used when it is delivered. If something fails, you get the credits back.

faq.q: Can I try it for free?
faq.a: There's no free plan right now. Plans start at $24.50 a month, and you see the credit cost of every photo or video before it's made, so you never spend more than you expect.

faq.q: How many videos and photos do I get each month?
faq.a: A product photo or a 6-second video uses 24 credits, a 10-second video 40 and a 15-second video 60. The Starter plan's 200 credits cover about eight photos or three 15-second videos a month.

faq.q: Is the person in the video a real creator?
faq.a: No. The people in AI UGC videos are generated by AI, so show the product with them rather than presenting the clip as a customer review. Some platforms ask you to label AI-generated content.

faq.q: Does it add voiceover or music?
faq.a: No. Add captions and music in TikTok or CapCut after you download, and type prices or offers in your editor or ad tool so every word is exactly right.
Yes. If you cancel, you keep the credits you've already bought until they're used or expire under your plan's rules. Credits that were already used aren't refunded.
